title: Wallet transfer in one unit of work
problem: wallet.py moves money between accounts. Finish it so a transfer is all or nothing: a UnitOfWork context manager owns the transaction, the repository never commits, and withdrawing can't overdraw even under concurrency. One repository method already has a bug that breaks the all-or-nothing rule: find it.
requirements: No AccountRepo method commits; the UnitOfWork decides
AccountRepo.withdraw uses one conditional UPDATE and returns whether a row changed
UnitOfWork: __enter__ returns the unit of work; __exit__ commits on success, rolls back on an exception and lets the exception propagate
transfer validates input (ValueError), then runs all reads and writes inside one UnitOfWork
transfer raises AccountNotFound or InsufficientFunds, and no balance changes on any error
contract:
AccountRepo(conn).withdraw(account_id: int, amount: int) -> bool
with UnitOfWork(conn) as uow: uow.accounts.deposit(...)
transfer(conn, from_id: int, to_id: int, amount: int) -> None
expectedBehavior: With balances {1: 100, 2: 0}: transfer(conn, 1, 2, 30) gives {1: 70, 2: 30}. transfer(conn, 1, 99, 10) raises AccountNotFound and leaves {1: 100, 2: 0}, even if the withdraw already ran.
edgeCases: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance succeeds; one more fails
Destination account missing after the source was already debited: everything rolls back
amount 0 or negative, and transferring to the same account: ValueError with no change
An exception inside the with block must reach the caller unchanged (not swallowed)
hints: Conceptual: a transaction belongs to the use case (the transfer), not to each SQL statement. If any single method commits, a later failure can't undo it. Look for the line that does exactly that.

Specific: put the balance check into the UPDATE itself: change the row only WHERE the balance is high enough, then look at cursor.rowcount to see whether it happened. That closes the read-then-write gap.

Implementation: __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) receives exc_type None on success. Call self.conn.commit() or self.conn.rollback() accordingly and return False so Python re-raises the exception. In transfer, validate first, then open `with UnitOfWork(conn) as uow:` and raise the domain errors inside it.
evaluation: withdraw is a single conditional UPDATE, not a SELECT followed by an UPDATE
Domain errors are raised inside the with block so the rollback happens
